request.body: no body; one GET of the RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata path for the issuer https://mcp.zendesk.com/api/mcp/oauth, the authorization server the protected-resource document of (Z2) names. User-agent public-agents-ci, no Authorization header, no cookie jar. Section (Z3) of the artifact, sent 12:04:58Z

decoded.document: 547 bytes: issuer https://mcp.zendesk.com/api/mcp/oauth; authorization_endpoint .../authorize; token_endpoint .../token; registration_endpoint .../register; response_types_supported code; grant_types_supported authorization_code and refresh_token; code_challenge_methods_supported S256; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported none; scopes_supported read and write.
decoded.what-it-means: a complete public-client OAuth stack for an MCP resource: PKCE S256, no client secret at the token endpoint, and a dynamic client registration endpoint, so a client that is not already registered can register itself. That is the opposite of the GitHub and HubSpot MCP servers in this registry, which publish no registration_endpoint, and the same shape as PostHog, GrowthBook, Convert, Optimizely and Statsig.
decoded.control: the control is the same path on an invented account host, section (Z6): 200, 607 bytes, the same nine fields with the invented hostname in every URL, registration endpoint included. So the document is minted per hostname by the platform and does not say the host is an account.
decoded.not-sent: no registration was attempted: POST /api/mcp/oauth/register would create a client record on the vendor's side, which is state and not a probe. A GET of that path, section (Z9), answers 401 with a Zendesk error envelope and no challenge, which is what a POST-only endpoint answers a GET and is not a reading of registration. The path-first form of the metadata URL, /api/mcp/oauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, answers the same 401 envelope (12:04Z, logged by status and not archived).
decoded.not-measured: whether registration succeeds, what the authorize endpoint renders, whether tokens are account-scoped; whether any vendor page describes this issuer (none found 12:05Z).

finding: The authorization server that Zendesk's undocumented /api/mcp endpoint names publishes RFC 8414 metadata keyless: PKCE S256, authorization-code and refresh-token grants, token endpoint auth none, scopes read and write, and a registration_endpoint at /api/mcp/oauth/register, so dynamic client registration is advertised. The same document, with the hostname substituted, is served for an invented account host (control record p-20261011-zendesk-api-mcp-invented-host-control, section Z6), so it is the platform's template and not one host's configuration. Registration was not attempted because it writes state on the vendor's side. The vendor documents none of this on any page found; the cache-control header says the document may be cached for an hour.
